I would highly recommend this app to anyone focused on self-development, discipline, productivity, or building healthier routines.

title: Almost perfect
body:
Grit has frankly astonished me, as someone who has downloaded hundreds of planner and todo apps, but never actually stuck with one. It is very easy and quick to add your habits and tasks. There are a good number of different tracking inputs too; I particularly appreciate the built in timers. I also love how you can enter in one time tasks much more easily and efficiently than in many other habit trackers. I never understood why anyone would want a separate app JUST for repeating tasks but that might just be me. There are two small changes that would make the app perfect for me. The first would be a setting whereby the tasks/habits that you create automatically adopt the colour and icon from their primary “group”, so I would no longer have to manually make everything match. Secondly, a system of tags, similar to the way groups work, would be useful for categorisation, enabling me to group a habit as “personal” but also tag it as “health” related, without it appearing twice on the dashboard/task list. In other words, a user would then be able to categorise a habit or task by its type (habit, bad habit, one off task) using the groups feature and have it appear as that in the dashboard, but also be able to describe it by its actual function or purpose as well through use of individual user created ‘tags’.

I really appreciate the app, and while I’m sure that there are probably bigger issues and lots of bugs that need fixing before adding any additional features, I really hope you take on my feedback!

title: Useful app with some caveats
body:
An extremely versatile and useful productivity app. It has a sleek layout, all the tasks are presented well and it even has widgets if you don't want to go on the app for whatever reason. However, there are apparent flaws. There is no separate section to distinct habits and todo lists (for that day) so things can get very cluttered, of course, you also need to pay for premium for full use of the app, but that's to be expected. 

I think a feature that would drastically improve the app and motivation to complete habits would be a leaderboard system where you can invite friends to your group and you can all see how many habits you've completed and compete kind of like habitshare.

title: Awesome app and outstanding support!
body:
I’ve been using Grit for barely a couple of weeks, but I can happily say I will be using it long-term. 

I recently started needing to log medication multiple times a day, along with wanting to track some other regular habits. I must have tried nearly two dozen apps and not a single one did everything I wanted, including this one. However, I put in a couple of feature requests and the developer, Stephan, implemented them in less than 24hrs. I have since made some more complex requests and these have been added too! 

The app itself is a joy to use. At first glance, it may seem quite simple, but everything that’s needed is there with no unnecessary clutter. It’s very easy to add positive and negative habits with varying frequencies. You can also add habits without a goal, great if you simply want to track something. 

The main statistics screen for each habit is very clean. It’s easy to see progress (and failures!) on the colourful calendar and there is an info box which highlights key data. My favourite section is the performance charts - these show your stats for selectable time periods, both as a total figure and a percentage. What I love is that you can clearly see when you’ve exceeded a habit goal as well as just achieving it. Very motivational!

I am very happy to have found this little app. It’s pretty much perfect for my needs now. I would perhaps like to see the Watch app fleshed out a bit more and the option to customise the widgets, but that’s nitpicking and I’m sure Stephan has plenty of ideas for the future. :)
